source_document: A People's History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn

claims.claim: History writing is never neutral but always shaped by ideological choices that reinforce power structures of the time
claims.supporting_evidence: Central methodological argument throughout the text
claims.relevance: Framework for critical analysis of official narratives

claims.claim: The concept of 'national interest' is a pretense masking the reality that America has always been divided by class, race, and economic interests
claims.supporting_evidence: Documented class conflicts throughout American history
claims.relevance: Critical lens for examining intelligence community claims of national security

claims.claim: Government economic policies are primarily directed towards the needs of corporations, with 'the economy' serving as shorthand for corporate profit
claims.supporting_evidence: Pattern of regulatory capture and corporate influence documented

claims.claim: Colonial America established economic and social structures that created persistent inequality and class struggle
claims.supporting_evidence: Extensive historical documentation of colonial class systems
claims.relevance: Foundation for understanding elite power networks

claims.claim: Major social progress (fair wages, labor laws, suffrage, civil rights) came from grassroots movements against bloody resistance from elites
claims.supporting_evidence: Documented history of labor movement, civil rights movement, suffrage movement
claims.relevance: Pattern of institutional resistance to reform

claims.claim: Traditional history teaching emphasizes 'great men in high places' while ignoring perspectives of workers, minorities, and marginalized groups
claims.supporting_evidence: Analysis of pre-1980 history curricula confirms this bias

claims.claim: America was built on the blood and suffering of the poor
claims.supporting_evidence: Extensive documentation of exploitation, though critics argue oversimplification
claims.relevance: Foundational critique of American exceptionalism narratives

claims.claim: Elite rulers from across orthodox political parties form an aggregate that manipulates and exploits the majority through rigged systems
claims.supporting_evidence: Documented cases of bipartisan elite cooperation
claims.relevance: HIGH - Directly applicable to Sherlock research on hidden power networks

cross_references.description: Wall Street-government nexus exemplifies Zinn's claims about elite power networks
CIA-Wall Street connections support claims about corporate-government alignment
